records.summary: The new reserve function has a concurrency bug because the check-and-update is not protected by the lock, and it also accepts non-positive quantities.

findings.title: Unprotected check-then-act allows overselling
findings.explanation: reserve reads stock, checks availability, and writes back without acquiring _lock, so concurrent threads can both pass the check and decrement the same stock, causing overselling or negative inventory. Wrap the read-check-write sequence in `with _lock:`.

records.summary: The new config loader silently swallows all load errors, leaks the opened file handle, and does not validate that the loaded JSON is a dict.

findings.title: All config load errors are silently swallowed
findings.explanation: The docstring says the function should raise if the file is missing or invalid, but the broad except Exception returns an empty dict instead. This can hide missing or malformed configuration and cause subtle downstream failures. Fix: remove the try/except or catch only specific errors such as OSError and json.JSONDecodeError and re-raise them.

findings.title: File handle is not explicitly closed
findings.explanation: open(path) is used without a context manager, so the file object is not explicitly closed. This is a resource-management issue and can leak file descriptors in some environments. Fix: use with open(path) as f: return json.load(f).

findings.title: Function may return a non-dict JSON value
findings.explanation: json.load can return any JSON value, such as a list or string, but the function is annotated to return dict. Callers expecting a mapping may fail unexpectedly. Fix: load the data, verify isinstance(data, dict), and raise a clear error otherwise.

records.summary: The new webhook verification code has a critical empty-secret fallback and uses a non-constant-time signature comparison.

findings.title: Empty default webhook secret allows signature forgery
findings.explanation: WEBHOOK_SECRET is initialized to b"" and only a comment says it is loaded from env. If the secret is not actually loaded, HMAC is computed with an empty key and an attacker can generate valid signatures. Load the secret from environment/config at startup and fail closed if it is missing or empty.

findings.title: Signature comparison is not constant-time
findings.explanation: Using expected == signature can leak timing information about the HMAC digest. Use hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature) to compare the values in constant time.

findings.explanation: requests.get(url) will fetch any user-controlled URL, including internal hosts, loopback addresses, link-local cloud metadata endpoints, or other restricted network targets. records.summary: The new billing client has payment-safety and error-handling issues: it can double-charge on timeout, treats HTTP errors as success, and has minor retry flaws.

findings.title: Retrying timed-out POST can duplicate charges
findings.explanation: A timeout may occur after the payment service has already processed the charge. Retrying the same POST without an idempotency key can create a second charge. Add a unique idempotency key to the request or avoid retrying ambiguous timeouts.

findings.title: HTTP error responses are returned as success
findings.explanation: The function returns r.json() without checking r.status_code, so 4xx/5xx error payloads are treated as successful charge results. Call r.raise_for_status() or explicitly handle non-2xx responses.

findings.title: Only timeouts are retried
findings.explanation: The docstring says transient network failures are retried, but requests.ConnectionError and other transient failures are not caught and will propagate. Catch the intended transient exceptions, while still using idempotency for POST retries.

findings.title: Unnecessary sleep after final attempt
findings.explanation: The loop sleeps after the third timeout before exiting and raising, adding 4 seconds of latency. Sleep only when another attempt will be made, e.g. if attempt < 2.

records.summary: The new pagination query is parameterized but has a correctness issue with timestamp ties and a potential unbounded-query issue if limit is negative.

findings.title: Cursor pagination can skip or duplicate posts with equal created_at
findings.explanation: Using only created_at as the cursor and ordering only by created_at is not deterministic when multiple posts share the same timestamp. Posts with the same created_at as the cursor may be omitted or repeated across pages. Fix by including id in the cursor and predicate, e.g. WHERE (created_at, id) < (?, ?) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC.

findings.title: Negative limit can disable the LIMIT clause
findings.explanation: If a caller passes a negative limit, SQLite may treat LIMIT -1 as no limit, causing an unbounded query. Fix by validating and clamping limit to a positive value, e.g. limit = max(1, min(limit, 100)).

findings.title: WEBHOOK_SECRET is not validated
findings.explanation: os.environ['WEBHOOK_SECRET'] raises if unset and accepts an empty string; an empty HMAC key allows an attacker to compute valid signatures. Load the secret, reject missing or empty values, and fail closed.

findings.title: Signature does not prevent replay
findings.explanation: The HMAC covers only the body, so a previously signed request can be replayed indefinitely. Include a timestamp or nonce in the signed payload and validate freshness when verifying.

records.summary: The PR simplifies path resolution in StaticResource by removing the lexical path-containment check that was applied when follow_symlinks=True. This removes the defense against directory traversal (e.g. ../ sequences in the filename) in that code path, since the new code calls .resolve() without ever verifying the result stays within the static directory.

findings.title: Path traversal check removed when follow_symlinks=True
findings.explanation: When follow_symlinks is True, the old code lexically normalised the path and called relative_to(self._directory) to reject filenames containing ../ that would escape the static directory. The new code calls .resolve() directly with no containment check, so a filename like '../../etc/passwd' resolves to a path outside the directory and is served. Fix: after resolving, verify containment, e.g. filepath.relative_to(self._directory.resolve()), or retain the pre-resolve lexical check.

findings.title: Path traversal check removed when follow_symlinks=True (second site)
findings.explanation: Same regression as line 122 in the _resolve method: when follow_symlinks is True the resolved path is never checked to be inside self._directory, allowing directory traversal via ../ in the filename or via a symlink that points outside the static root. records.summary: The PR simplifies StaticResource path resolution but drops the lexical containment check that was applied in the follow_symlinks=True branch. As a result, when follow_symlinks=True the resolved path is never verified to stay inside the static directory, so ../ (or an absolute path) in the request resolves outside the directory and is served/read. This is a path-traversal regression in both _handle and url_for.

findings.title: Path traversal when follow_symlinks=True in _handle
findings.explanation: With follow_symlinks=True the code does filepath = self._directory.joinpath(filename).resolve() and then skips the filepath.relative_to(self._directory) check (it only runs when not self._follow_symlinks). A request such as GET /static/../../etc/passwd (or percent-encoded %2e%2e, which _unquote_path decodes after routing) resolves to /etc/passwd and is returned via FileResponse, i.e. arbitrary file read. The removed os.path.normpath + relative_to check on the unresolved path is exactly what previously blocked this (it also blocked absolute-path injection like /static//etc/passwd). Fix: when follow_symlinks is True, still verify the lexically-normalized unresolved path (Path(os.path.normpath(self._directory.joinpath(filename))).relative_to(self._directory)) is contained before resolving, or otherwise reject any path that escapes the directory.

findings.title: Same path traversal in url_for with append_version
findings.explanation: The identical regression exists in url_for: with follow_symlinks=True and append_version=True, a filename containing ../ (or an absolute path) resolves outside self._directory, the containment check is skipped, and the file is opened and fully read into memory (f.read()) to compute a hash. This leaks a content hash for arbitrary files and risks memory exhaustion on large files if the filename is influenced by user input. Fix: apply the same lexical containment check on the unresolved path before resolving/reading, mirroring the _handle fix.

records.summary: The PR removes the `UnsafeOptionsUsedError` exception and all associated safety checks that prevented the use of dangerous git protocols (e.g. `ext::`) and options (e.g. `--upload-pack`, `--config protocol.*`) in `Repo.clone()` and `Repo.clone_from()`. This re-exposes the library to arbitrary command execution via crafted URLs or options.

findings.title: Unsafe protocol/option validation removed from Repo.clone()
findings.explanation: The `clone()` method previously called `self.unsafe_options(path, multi_options)` and raised `UnsafeOptionsUsedError` when the URL contained `ext::` or `multi_options` included `--upload-pack` or `--config protocol.*`. These checks are now gone, so a caller passing an attacker-controlled URL (e.g. `ext::sh -c 'malicious'`) or options will silently invoke `git clone` with arbitrary command execution. Restore the validation (or an equivalent allow-list) before delegating to `_clone`.

findings.title: Unsafe protocol/option validation removed from Repo.clone_from()
findings.explanation: The `clone_from()` classmethod had the same guard (`cls.unsafe_options(url, multi_options)`) which is now removed. Any code path that calls `Repo.clone_from(url, ...)` with an untrusted `url` or `multi_options` can trigger arbitrary command execution via `ext::` or `--upload-pack`. Restore the check before the `cls._clone(...)` call.

findings.title: Public exception class removed without deprecation
findings.explanation: `UnsafeOptionsUsedError` was a public exception that downstream code may catch. Removing it outright (rather than deprecating first) will cause `ImportError`/`NameError` in any consumer that references it. If the security check is intentionally being removed, the exception should be deprecated in a prior release; if it is being kept, the class must not be deleted.

records.summary: The PR removes GitPython's unsafe protocol/options guard for clone operations, re-exposing arbitrary command execution via ext:: URLs and --upload-pack/-c protocol.* options, and also breaks the public unsafe_protocols/UnsafeOptionsUsedError API.

findings.title: clone_from no longer rejects unsafe protocols or options
findings.explanation: The removed unsafe_options check allowed ext:: URLs and multi_options containing --upload-pack or -c protocol.* to be passed directly to git clone, enabling arbitrary command execution or unsafe protocol use. Restore validation of url and multi_options before calling cls._clone, or require an explicit unsafe_protocols flag and raise UnsafeOptionsUsedError.

findings.title: Repo.clone no longer validates multi_options
findings.explanation: Removing the unsafe_options check lets callers pass --upload-pack or -c protocol.* options to git clone for a local repository, which can still execute arbitrary programs or enable unsafe protocols. Validate multi_options before self._clone or restore the unsafe_protocols guard.

findings.title: Public unsafe_protocols API removed
findings.explanation: clone and clone_from no longer accept unsafe_protocols, and UnsafeOptionsUsedError is removed, so existing callers passing the flag or catching the exception will fail. If this is intentional, document the breaking change or keep a deprecated alias/parameter.

records.summary: The PR replaces the robust is_pem_format/is_ssh_key helpers with a hardcoded substring check and restructures EdDSA key loading. This weakens HMAC key validation (private keys and most PEM/SSH formats are no longer rejected), removes the EdDSA post-load type check so non-Ed PEM keys are accepted and fail later with confusing errors, and changes the raised exception from InvalidKeyError to TypeError.

findings.title: HMAC key check no longer rejects private keys or most PEM/SSH formats
findings.explanation: The hardcoded list only matches 4 markers, so PEM private keys (PRIVATE KEY, RSA/EC/DSA PRIVATE KEY, ENCRYPTED/OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY) and non-RSA SSH keys (ssh-ed25519, ecdsa-sha2-nistp*, etc.) are no longer detected and can be silently used as HMAC secrets. Restore detection of all key types (e.g., match any '-----BEGIN ... KEY/CERTIFICATE' header, or keep the removed is_pem_format/is_ssh_key helpers).

findings.title: EdDSA prepare_key accepts non-Ed PEM keys
findings.explanation: The post-load isinstance check was removed, so an RSA/EC PEM key passed to EdDSAAlgorithm is loaded and returned successfully, then fails later in sign/verify with a confusing cryptography error instead of a clear InvalidKeyError. After loading, verify the key is an Ed key and raise InvalidKeyError otherwise.

findings.title: EdDSA prepare_key raises TypeError instead of InvalidKeyError
findings.explanation: Invalid keys now raise TypeError rather than InvalidKeyError (a PyJWTError subclass), so callers catching InvalidKeyError/PyJWTError will no longer handle this case. Raise InvalidKeyError to preserve the public exception contract.

records.summary: The change removes the guard that prevented adding Proxy-Authorization headers for HTTPS proxy requests, which can leak proxy credentials to the target server.

findings.title: Proxy credentials leaked to target server for HTTPS proxy requests
findings.explanation: Removing the `not scheme.startswith('https')` check causes `Proxy-Authorization` to be added to request headers for HTTPS requests through an authenticated proxy. After the CONNECT tunnel is established, that header can be sent to the destination server, exposing the proxy username and password. Restore the scheme check or only add the header for non-HTTPS proxy schemes.

The change replaces object_hook-based untagging with a post-parse recursive scan. This is functionally similar but adds an extra traversal and container copies for every JSON load.

findings.title: Post-parse untag scan adds extra traversal and allocations
findings.explanation: loads now parses the entire JSON document and then recursively rebuilds every dict and list before untagging. Compared with object_hook=self.untag, this adds a second pass and extra memory/CPU cost for large payloads. If the post-parse scan is not required for correctness, keep object_hook; otherwise implement the scan iteratively or avoid copying containers that do not need untagging.

records.summary: Making --cert eager changes option-processing order and can cause certificate validation to run before --help.

findings.title: Eager --cert can prevent --help from working
findings.explanation: Click processes eager options before the appended --help option. If CertParamType.convert fails for a nonexistent certificate file, commands like `flask run --cert missing --help` will raise a usage error instead of showing help. Avoid is_eager unless required, or defer certificate validation to the command callback.
